papers.title_en: VidEdit3D: Flexible 3D Gaussian Editing with Video Diffusion
papers.authors: Yanming Yang, Chenxi Song, Tong Zhao, Juntao Xu, Wenhao Rao, Yiwen Chen, Yiwei Wang, Chi Zhang
papers.evidence: 基于3D高斯泼溅的多视角一致场景编辑
papers.tldr: 针对文本引导3D高斯编辑中多视角一致性与结构修改难以兼得、非常规视角编辑不稳定的问题，VidEdit3D将静态3D场景编辑重构为轨迹驱动的视频编辑任务，借助预训练视频扩散模型的时空先验传播锚点编辑。方法包含轨迹引导渲染、流对齐视频编辑与区域选择式3DGS精修。实验显示其指令对齐和多视角一致性优于基线。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advancements in text-guided 3D editing, particularly with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), have shown promise but still lag behind the flexibility of 2D editing tools. Existing methods face a critical trade-off between preserving multi-view consistency and allowing structural modifications. Image-based editors can also struggle to apply the intended edit to objects viewed from unusual angles. To address these limitations, we introduce VidEdit3D, a framework that reformulates 3D scene editing as a trajectory-based video editing task. By drawing a parallel between camera movement in static 3D scenes and temporal dynamics in video, we leverage the robust spatiotemporal priors of pre-trained Video Diffusion Models (VDMs) to encourage semantic and structural coherence across views. Specifically, we propose Trajectory-Guided Rendering (TGR) to select informative keyframes and construct smooth video clips aligned with VDM input requirements. To propagate edits from an anchor view to these clips, we develop Flow-Aligned Video Editing (FAVE), a training-free framework incorporating an Editing Consistency Guidance (ECG) mechanism. ECG contrasts source and edited image conditions at a shared latent state, using scheduled source-image amplification to strengthen adherence to the edited reference while maintaining original scene context. Finally, we introduce Region-Selective 3DGS Refinement (RS-GS) to strictly confine geometric and appearance updates to target primitives, reducing background attribute leakage. Experiments demonstrate stronger instruction alignment and better multi-view consistency than the baselines.

papers.title_en: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
papers.authors: Jinhyeok Choi, JoungBin Lee, Jongmin Lee, Minkyeong Jeon, Jiyoung Kim, Kaeun Han, Yoonjin Yoon, Seungryong Kim
papers.evidence: 以潜在3D高斯记忆作为紧凑可渲染场景表征
papers.tldr: 交互式世界模型需实时生成长时程一致内容，但时序上下文和显式3D记忆随流长度膨胀，且重编码RGB阻碍实时性。L3G-World提出潜在3D高斯记忆L3G，以可快速渲染的紧凑场景表示存储VAE潜在特征，并由记忆更新器与视频DiT自回归交替生成。实验在生成质量与长时程空间一致性上达SOTA，3D基元最多少38.6倍、更新快3.2倍、渲染快359倍，实现9 FPS实时世界生成。
papers.abstract_en: Interactive world models generate visual content conditioned on user actions, yet maintaining spatial consistency over long-horizon exploration in real time remains challenging. Existing approaches rely on either temporal context or explicit 3D memory, both of which scale poorly because memory grows with the length of the generated stream. Moreover, explicit 3D memories condition latent video generators by re-encoding RGB renderings, which precludes real-time generation. In this paper, we introduce a Latent 3D Gaussian Memory (L3G) that combines the efficiency of feed-forward reconstruction with a compact, rapidly renderable scene representation. Building on this memory, we propose L3G-World, in which a memory updater and a video diffusion transformer (DiT) alternate autoregressively to generate spatially consistent worlds. The memory updater spawns Gaussians in newly observed regions and refines existing ones, so that the memory grows with scene extent rather than stream length. Each Gaussian further stores a VAE latent feature, allowing the memory to be rendered directly into the DiT's latent space without VAE re-encoding. Experiments show that L3G-World achieves state-of-the-art generation quality and long-horizon spatial consistency, with up to $38.6\times$ fewer 3D primitives, $3.2\times$ faster memory updates, and $359\times$ faster memory rendering relative to the most efficient prior 3D-memory baseline for each metric, enabling real-time world generation at 9 FPS.
